codeReview.summary: The fix tightens the detection heuristics and corrects most of the researched container/component commands, but it does not fully resolve the prior blocking toolchain-alignment issue. Python builds still invoke componentize-py with a filename such as app.py instead of the documented module-name form, and the new tests still bypass the real container/timeout paths that were meant to guard these command strings.

issues.description: buildPythonComponentize now switches to wasi:http/proxy, but it still feeds componentize-py the filename returned by findPythonAppModule (for example app.py or main.py). The documented command in docs/wasm-language-support-research.md is componentize-py -d wit -w wasi:http/proxy componentize app -o app.wasm, i.e. a module name, not a .py path. Because findPythonAppModule returns filenames (see the helper at lines 498-512), the Python component build path is still misaligned with the researched toolchain and can fail for the advertised language support.

The added build-path coverage still does not exercise the risky paths that changed in this fix. The new tests explicitly set JANUS_BUILD_NO_CONTAINER=1, so they only hit host-mode fallbacks and never verify the real container command construction, and TestBuildTimeout_ContextCancelled only checks that a cancelled context returns some error instead of asserting the timeout snippet emitted by workflow.go. That leaves the containerized command wiring and timeout-reporting contract weakly covered.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker procedure has no equivalent of API manual verification for non-API infrastructure changes such as containerized build command wiring, so a worker can mark followedProcedure=true after only unit-test coverage even when the change hinges on an external tool invocation string.
